Root Cause Diagnosis                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                        
### What the test expects                                                                                               
                                                                                                                        
test_process_order_succeeds() (sample-target/tests/test_app.py:3) calls process_order(101) (sample-target/app.py:4) and 
asserts that the returned dict has status == "success". It assumes the function always succeeds — no branching, no      
mocking, no retry.                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                        
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                        
                                                                                                                        
### What the code actually does                                                                                         
                                                                                                                        
process_order() (sample-target/app.py:4) has two lines that introduce non-determinism:                                  
                                                                                                                        
```python                                                                                                               
  delay = random.uniform(0, 0.3)   # line 6 — random float in [0.0, 0.3)                                                
  time.sleep(delay)                 # line 7 — blocks for that duration                                                 
  if delay > 0.2:                   # line 8 — the branch that kills the test                                           
      return {"status": "timeout"}                                                                                      
  return {"status": "success", "order_id": order_id}                                                                    
```                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                        
1. random.uniform(0, 0.3) — draws a uniformly distributed float from the range [0.0, 0.3] on every call. There is no    
   fixed seed, so the result is different each run.                                                                     
2. The > 0.2 threshold — any sampled value above 0.2 takes the early-return path and returns {"status": "timeout"}      
   instead of {"status": "success"}.                                                                                    
                                                                                                                        
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                        
                                                                                                                        
### Why the test is flaky                                                                                               
                                                                                                                        
The range (0.0, 0.3] is split into two zones:                                                                           
                                                                                                                        
┌───────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────────┐                                                                 
│ Range     │ Result       │ Width                    │                                                                 
├───────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────────────┤                                                                 
│ 0.0 – 0.2 │ "success" ✅ │ 0.2 / 0.3 = ~67% of runs │                                                                 
├───────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────────────┤                                                                 
│ 0.2 – 0.3 │ "timeout" ❌ │ 0.1 / 0.3 = ~33% of runs │                                                                 
└───────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────────┘                                                                 
                                                                                                                        
Roughly one in three test runs will draw a delay above 0.2, hit the "timeout" branch, and cause the assertion           
result["status"] == "success" to fail. The other two-thirds pass normally.                                              
                                                                                                                        
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                        
                                                                                                                        
### The core issue in one sentence                                                                                      
                                                                                                                        
The test exercises a function whose return value is decided by an unseeded random call at runtime, and the test asserts 
only the happy-path outcome — making it non-deterministic by design, with approximately a 33% failure rate per          
execution.
